configuration.lag_sign_convention: lag = k pairs oil from week (t - k) with interest at week t; k > 0 means oil leads interest

specifications.description: Weekly levels, as published. The primary specification.
Week-over-week changes. Removes any shared trend, but is noisy and has low power when the true relationship operates on levels.
Residuals after removing a linear time trend from each series. Only a straight line is removed, so a flat-then-step price path is not fully detrended by this specification.

trend_diagnostics.note: Two series that both trend upward across a window will correlate in levels whether or not they are related. First differences test week-to-week co-movement; detrended residuals remove a linear trend only, which models a flat-then-step price path poorly. Neither check is decisive on its own, so all three specifications are reported and their disagreement is treated as a finding rather than resolved by choosing a favourite.

variants.description: Weeks whose oil mean came from fewer than 5 trading days are removed.
Only weeks before the price-regime onset (2026-03-01) are used.
Only weeks from the price-regime onset (2026-03-01) onward are used.
Spearman rank correlation, which limits the leverage of extreme values.

category_review.basis: Asserts that Indonesian interest is insulated from oil-price movement, which predicts no detectable association. Observed: indonesia measured as 'no_detectable_association'.

Asserts that both markets pivot quickly and strongly with oil-price pressure, which predicts a positive association that survives differencing. Observed: malaysia measured as 'inconclusive', us measured as 'level_only_association'.

Asserts Norwegian saturation (no association) alongside Singaporean responsiveness constrained by adoption barriers (a positive association). Observed: norway measured as 'no_detectable_association', singapore measured as 'level_only_association'.
